clue.text: US sex worker gets with Hoskins in a cottage?

parts.note: ho is American slang for a prostitute
Hoskins is the setter, so the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A tawdry tale of a streetwalker and the setter shacking up together in a country cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often name themselves in clues; Hoskins is this puzzle's setter, so the self-reference gives ME. The question mark flags that a cottage is only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is one kind of dwelling where people live, so it is an example of a domestic residence.

clue.text: Oscar rejected wicked name for a baby girl?

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: what is rejected is sent back, so the word is turned the other way round

parts.note: wicked and evil are synonyms

explanation.surface: Someone called Oscar vetoes a sinister-sounding name proposed for a newborn daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar looks like a person in the surface, but it is just the letter O from the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a familiar female first name, so parents could choose it when naming their daughter.

clue.text: After getting on beers, old husband expires

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on top of something means coming before it in the column

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
H is the abbreviation for husband
ales are beers

explanation.surface: A former husband drinks one beer too many and dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expires' tempts the reader to think of death, which suits the drunken surface, but here it is the literal sense of breathing out.
explanation.definitionFit: To expire in its original physiological sense is to breathe air out of the lungs.

clue.text: Roofer or hairdresser, might some people say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a craftsman who roofs cottages with straw or reeds
second meaning: thatch is jokey slang for a head of hair, so a hair stylist could be called this

explanation.walkthrough: Thatch is informal British slang for a thick head of hair, so the second meaning is a playful extension, hedged by 'might some people say'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the trade name for someone laying straw roofs, and jokingly fits a person who tends a mop of hair.

clue.text: Earl has intercourse upside-down in restraint

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something upside down makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for Earl
'it' is a coy euphemism for sex, so Earl has it

explanation.surface: A saucy picture of an aristocrat engaged in kinky, inverted bondage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' joins the Earl to the euphemism 'it' (sex), and the pair is then flipped as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is anything that binds or holds someone back, so it serves as a synonym for a curb.

clue.text: Paintings by The Spanish Cooperative in the USSR

parts.note: paintings are works of art
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: An exhibition of Spanish paintings mounted by a Soviet collective.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised 'The Spanish' looks like a title, but it simply asks for the Spanish word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artel was a Russian and Soviet workers' association whose members shared labour and profits.

clue.text: Cautious on turning right into group of a load of chickens?

indicators.note: one letter turns into another, so it is swapped out for its replacement

parts.note: cautious and careful are synonyms
R is the abbreviation for right
the first letter of group stands in for the word

explanation.surface: Someone tiptoes carefully around a flock of hens.
explanation.walkthrough: The R in CAREFUL becomes a G, giving CAGEFUL. The question mark admits it is an invented word: battery chickens are kept in cages.
explanation.definitionFit: A cageful is as many birds as one cage holds, so a quantity of poultry fills one.

clue.text: Church services still no good? Head to Satan!

parts.note: 'even so' means nevertheless, all the same
NG is the standard abbreviation for no good

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the devil's name

explanation.surface: A frustrated churchgoer finds services still useless and tells them to go to the devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' tempts you to EVEN, but it is the adverb meaning 'nevertheless', which is EVEN SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican service of evening prayer, so the plural names several such acts of worship.

clue.text: Remains drunk mostly, drinking a drop of grappa

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
whoever drinks takes something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: wrecked is slang for drunk, losing its last letter
taken as written

indicators.note: a drop is the smallest amount, so only an initial letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the Italian brandy

explanation.surface: Someone who is nearly paralytic stays on for one more sip of grappa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb about staying drunk, but it is the noun for what is left after destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreckage is the debris left after a crash or ruin, so it is what survives of something broken.

clue.text: Religious type spread right pish about ecstasy

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other
spreading things out scatters them, so the letters are laid out in a new order

parts.note: letters taken as written for rearranging
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A cleric spouts utter nonsense about the joys of rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: Pish is old-fashioned or Scots slang for nonsense; ecstasy can be read as rapture, but it is the drug, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A high priest is the chief cleric of a temple or faith, so is a person devoted to religion.

clue.text: Ancient German quarry excavating phosphorus

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German

indicators.note: excavating digs material out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: quarry is the animal hunted, its prey
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: Archaeologists dig phosphorus out of an old quarry in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarry' suggests a pit, which suits 'excavating', but it is the hunter's target.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey describes hair turned white with age, so it loosely means old or elderly.

clue.text: Go to get Liverpool's latest strip

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for to urinate, to pee

indicators.note: the latest of something is its last, so only the final letter counts

parts.note: the final letter of the city's name

explanation.surface: A fan heads off to buy the newest Liverpool football shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' looks like a football kit, but it is the verb meaning to remove an outer layer.
explanation.definitionFit: To peel is to take the skin or outer covering off, a synonym of to strip.

clue.text: Ink manufacturer is mixed up in fetish cult

indicators.note: things mixed up are jumbled together, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: letters taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A printing-ink company is implicated in a weird fetish cult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ink manufacturer' reads as a company, but it is a sea creature that squirts ink.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuttlefish squirts a dark fluid, sepia, to escape predators, so it literally produces ink.

clue.text: Grass up granny, perhaps, in Barnet do?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: grass and pot are both slang for cannabis
a granny is a kind of knot

explanation.surface: Someone informs on their grandmother over goings-on at a party in Barnet, a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass up' looks like British slang for informing, but grass is cannabis and 'up' turns it over. Barnet is rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair).
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a hairstyle with hair gathered into a bun on the crown, so it is a hairdo.

clue.text: Country type coming up on drugs on the radio?

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than read, so it is the sound that matters

parts.note: someone who is coming up on drugs feels a rush, making them a rusher

explanation.surface: A clubber feels the drugs kick in while a country-music song plays on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: To come up on drugs is to feel them start working, the rush; in a non-rhotic British accent, rusher and the country name sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is the largest nation on earth, spanning eastern Europe and northern Asia.

clue.text: Lend nude drunk clothes bishop kept in original state?

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so one piece wraps around another
a drunk staggers about, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: letters taken as written for rearranging
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A drunk lends clothes to a naked bishop so he can keep his dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun being lent, but it is a verb: the jumbled letters dress the bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not mixed with anything else stays pure, as it was, such as a single malt whisky.

clue.text: Light on other side of harbour in Oregon city

indicators.note: placed beyond something, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: a port is a harbour
to light on is to land on, settle

explanation.surface: A lighthouse beam shines across a harbour on the US Pacific coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like a noun for a lamp, but it is the verb meaning to alight or land.
explanation.definitionFit: Portland is the largest city in the US state of Oregon.

clue.text: Criminal ringing about evil leader in power

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other
something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: letters taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: a leader goes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of evil

explanation.surface: A crook phones round about a wicked tyrant who holds power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evil leader' suggests a despot, but it asks only for the first letter of evil.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who is reigning currently holds the throne and rules, so is in authority.

clue.text: Earned bucks screening Black Earth and Metropolis

indicators.note: a bucking horse throws itself about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: letters taken as written for rearranging
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
E is the abbreviation for Earth

explanation.surface: A cinema made money showing the classic films Black Earth and Metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bucks' reads as dollars earned, but it is a verb signalling the shuffle. Aberdeen is a city in north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is Scotland's third-largest city, so it is an urban centre of some size.

clue.text: Italian anatomist using some Demerol and opiates

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used, so the answer is a run inside the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of the painkiller, the whole of 'and' and the start of 'opiates'

explanation.surface: An Italian surgeon relies on painkillers such as Demerol and opiates.
explanation.walkthrough: Demerol is an American brand of the painkiller pethidine. Luigi Rolando was a 19th-century Italian who studied the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Rolando was an Italian anatomist after whom the fissure of Rolando in the brain is named.

clue.text: I will get new patient, if there happens to be a need

definitions.text: if there happens to be a need

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
doctors refer to a patient as a case

explanation.surface: A doctor promises to take on another patient should one require treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like an adjective meaning tolerant, but it is the noun, a person under medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a precaution against a possible eventuality, should something come to pass.

clue.text: Lawyer local authority brought into hearing

indicators.note: something brought into hearing is heard, so its sound gives the spelling

parts.note: a council is the body running a town or district

explanation.surface: A council employs a solicitor to appear at a legal hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' suggests a court session, which fits the lawyer, but it signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is the formal term for a barrister or advocate acting for a party in court.

clue.text: No gent will put out for an item of footwear

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed or upset, so its letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: letters taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A fussy remark that no gentleman will sleep with someone in exchange for a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as a crude phrase for consenting to sex, but it signals the rearrangement. A wellington is a rubber rain boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellington is a waterproof rubber boot named after the Duke of Wellington, so it is worn on the feet.

clue.text: Note-grabbing relatives will make some bread

indicators.note: grabbing something holds it inside a grip, so one piece takes in another

parts.note: nans are grandmothers
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: Grasping relatives snatch banknotes, hoping to make some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' and 'bread' both suggest cash, but one is a musical note and the other is food.
explanation.definitionFit: Naans are leavened flatbreads from South Asia, so several of them are loaves of a kind.

clue.text: Language of Monsieur Duchamp

indicators.note: a word made of others is drawn out from within their letters

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of the title and the start of the surname

explanation.walkthrough: The French setting suggests French, but the answer sits inside the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national tongue of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: Trance band who provided Blair's campaign tune

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dazed, absent state of mind

definitions.text: band who provided Blair's campaign tune
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the pop group whose 'Things Can Only Get Better' was Labour's 1997 election anthem

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trance' looks like a dance-music genre to go with the band, but it is a separate meaning. Tony Blair led Labour to victory in 1997 with D:Ream's song.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverie is a trance-like state, and D:Ream is the Northern Irish pop group behind the 1997 Labour anthem.

clue.text: Nurse getting on my boss will find paradise

explanation.walkthrough: EN stands for Enrolled Nurse, a British nursing grade; 'my boss' is the setter's editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical garden of Adam and Eve, used for any blissful place.

clue.text: Dispense with a dead person found in cabinet?

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for dead
the government cabinet is made up of ministers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests a piece of furniture where a corpse might be stashed, but it is the government's senior ministers.

clue.text: Old lady sat by gym nude in page on a calendar?

parts.note: the inner letter of gym

explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes a nude calendar shoot; 'nude' is just the stripping instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall calendar has one leaf per month, and the fifth month gets its own sheet.

clue.text: Lousy do I got going in an offensive way

explanation.definitionFit: Odiously means in a hateful, repugnant manner, so it describes conduct that gives offence.

clue.text: Jesus appears in clam bake!

indicators.note: what appears in some words is found sitting inside their letters

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of the shellfish and the start of the cooking

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a vision of Christ at a seafood barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jesus' reads like an oath, but it is the definition. A clambake is an American beach party where shellfish are cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ is called the Lamb of God in the Gospels, a title for the sacrificial saviour.
